observation.visible_scene: A brightly lit dance studio with white walls, a light wood floor, a dark ceiling fitted with track spotlights, a wall-mounted air-conditioning unit on the upper left, and a full-height mirror covering the right wall. A woman with long dark hair tied back, wearing a black floral dress with red trim and red leg warmers over heeled shoes, stands center-left facing the mirror and performs a slow arm choreography. Her front-facing image in the mirror is a reflection of the same dancer, not a second person. The camera is stationary throughout; background elements keep fixed positions.
visible_changes: At the start the dancer's right arm is bent and raised near her head while her left arm is extended outward to the side; this pose is held with only minor adjustments for the first several frames.
Around mid-segment the raised right fist lifts higher and the left arm sweeps forward/out as the torso rotates slightly toward the mirror.
The two arms then draw together in front of the chest/face, opening the palms, before folding/crossing at chest level for a brief interval.
After the crossed-arms interval the right arm bends across the body and points forward while the left hand rests on the hip.

Toward the end the right arm extends forward and then rises diagonally upward, while the left arm moves from the hip out to the side, ending in a high-arm, extended-arm pose different from the opening pose.
The mirror reflection reproduces every one of these arm and torso changes in real time, confirming it is the same dancer.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the dancer does before t=0 and after t=1.6 s is not shown; the opening and closing poses do not need to connect.
Whether the routine continues with steps or other movements is unknown.
No audio or music cues are visible.
uncertain_details: The exact dance style or named move is not identifiable from the frames.
Subtle weight shifts of the legs are minimal and not clearly tracked; feet stay roughly in place.
Camera motion is essentially absent, but tiny framing drift cannot be fully ruled out from stills alone.
